provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Graduation portfolio
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to select their best five artworks
The pupils should be able to mount and label their chosen works

Introduction:
We have made many beautiful art pieces this term.
Today we will choose our best works for our graduation portfolio.

Content:
Look at all your art works.
Pick five that make you happy.
These will be your best five works.
Mount them on clean paper.
Write your name on each one.

Class activity:
Each child will select five artworks.
They will mount them on colored paper.
They will write their names on each piece.

Evaluation questions:
What is a portfolio?
How many works should you choose?
What do you write on your mounted works?

Summary:
A graduation portfolio shows your best art works.

topics.title: Artist statement
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to talk about their art
The pupils should be able to write their artist line

Introduction:
Every artist tells people about their art.
Today we will learn to talk about our own art.

Content:
An artist statement is what you say about your art.
Think about what you made.
Why did you make it?
What colors did you use?
Your artist line is one sentence about your art.

Class activity:
Each child will stand up.
They will show one art work.
They will say one sentence about it.

Evaluation questions:
What is an artist statement?
What is an artist line?
Can you say your artist line?

Summary:
An artist statement tells about your art.

topics.title: Portfolio walk
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to present their portfolio to another class
The pupils should be able to answer questions about their art

Introduction:
We have made beautiful portfolios.
Today we will show them to another class.

Content:
A portfolio walk means showing your art.
Hold your portfolio nicely.
Walk carefully with it.
When people ask questions, answer them nicely.

Class activity:
The teacher will take the class to another classroom.
Each child will show their portfolio.
They will answer questions from other pupils.

Evaluation questions:
What is a portfolio walk?
How do you hold your portfolio?
What do you do when someone asks a question?

Summary:
A portfolio walk is showing your art to others.

topics.title: Community art gift
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to make art for the school wall
The pupils should be able to create a legacy mural tile

Introduction:
Our school is a special place.
Today we will make art to give to our school.

Content:
We will make a big mural for the school wall.
Each child will make one tile.
Draw something beautiful.
Use bright colors.
Your tile will be part of the school forever.

Class activity:
Each child will get a small tile.
They will draw something beautiful on it.
They will paint it with bright colors.
The teacher will put all tiles together.

Evaluation questions:
What are we making for the school?
What will you draw on your tile?
How long will your art stay in school?

Summary:
We are making a mural gift for our school.

topics.title: Gift crafts
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to make presents for parents
The pupils should be able to wrap presents with our paper

Introduction:
Our parents love us very much.
Today we will make gifts for them.

Content:
We will make special crafts for our parents.
Draw something your parents like.
Color it nicely.
Make a card for them too.
Wrap your gift in special paper.

Class activity:
Each child will make a craft.
They will draw and color a picture.
They will make a card.
They will wrap their gift.

Evaluation questions:
Who are you making gifts for?
What will you draw for your parents?
How will you wrap your gift?

Summary:
We are making special gifts for our parents.

topics.title: Memory book art
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to draw their nursery memories
The pupils should be able to create pages of their journey

Introduction:
We have been in nursery for three years.
Today we will draw our memories.

Content:
A memory book shows your time in nursery.
Draw your first day in nursery.
Draw your best friend in nursery.
Draw your favorite teacher.
Draw your favorite game.

Class activity:
Each child will get a paper book.
They will draw four pages of memories.
They will color their drawings.
They will share their books with friends.

Evaluation questions:
What is a memory book?
What memories will you draw?
How many pages will you make?

Summary:
A memory book shows your nursery journey.

topics.title: Class flag design
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to design a graduating flag
The pupils should be able to vote for the best design and help sew it

Introduction:
Every class has a special flag.
Today we will design our graduating flag.

Content:
A flag shows what our class loves.
Draw symbols of our class.
Use our school colors.
Think of something special about Nursery 3.
We will vote for the best design.
Then we will sew it together.

Class activity:
Each child will draw a flag design.
The class will vote for the best one.
The teacher will help sew the winning flag.

Evaluation questions:
What is a class flag?
What should you draw on our flag?
What will we do after voting?

Summary:
We will design and make our class flag.

topics.title: Stage craft final
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to help with final stage dressing
The pupils should be able to arrange curtains and flowers

Introduction:
Our graduation is coming soon.
Today we will make our stage beautiful.

Content:
Stage craft means making the stage ready.
We will put up curtains.
We will arrange flowers.
We will make sure everything is in place.
The stage must look nice for our graduation.

Class activity:
The children will help put up curtains.
They will arrange flowers around the stage.
They will check that everything is ready.

Evaluation questions:
What is stage craft?
What will we put on the stage?
Why do we make the stage nice?

Summary:
We are making our stage beautiful for graduation.

topics.title: Grand rehearsal
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to participate in full dress rehearsal
The pupils should be able to take their correct positions

Introduction:
Our graduation is almost here.
Today we will practice everything.

Content:
A rehearsal is practice for the real thing.
Full dress rehearsal means wearing our graduation clothes.
We will walk to the stage.
We will say our lines.
We will sing our songs.
Everyone must know their place.

Class activity:
The children will wear their graduation clothes.
They will walk to the stage as practiced.
They will do everything as if it is the real day.

Evaluation questions:
What is a rehearsal?
What is full dress rehearsal?
Why is it important to know your place?

Summary:
We are practicing for our graduation day.

topics.title: Graduation day art
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to display their art on graduation day
The pupils should be able to feel proud of their work

Introduction:
Graduation day is our special day.
Today we will show our best art.

Content:
On graduation day we wear our best clothes.
We put our art on display.
Parents and teachers will see our work.
We will feel proud of what we made.
Our art shows how much we have learned.

Class activity:
The children will arrange their art on tables.
They will stand next to their work.
They will explain their art to visitors.

Evaluation questions:
What do we wear on graduation day?
Where will we put our art?
How should we feel about our work?

Summary:
On graduation day we proudly show our art.
